artifacts.summary: Pinpoints the exact Site-2 strip block in git-commit-phase.sh and the exact insertion point inside git-commit-scoped.sh's V10 containment_scope_arr assembly, the variable-rename and warn()-convention pitfalls, and the test-suite changes needed (restore Case 26's full assertion, add a new Z19 case, re-run Case 20 as a non-regression check).

memory_candidates.content: git-commit-scoped.sh's V10 containment_scope_arr is populated from the task's raw file_scope (a `while IFS= read -r s; do containment_scope_arr+=("$s"); done` loop reading jq '.[]' output) immediately followed by `if [ "${#containment_scope_arr[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then` which gates the own-task-directory/engine-written-state/derived-output widening splices. Any scope-definition filter (e.g. a deployed-tree strip) must be inserted strictly between the raw-population loop and that length guard, never inside it after the splices -- otherwise the guard evaluates against the unstripped array and a scope that should strip to empty incorrectly survives into the widening block.

git-commit-scoped.sh has no warn() helper function -- every V9/V10/V13 warning in that script is an inline `echo "WARN: git-commit-scoped.sh ..." >&2`. git-commit-phase.sh, by contrast, defines and uses a warn() helper. Porting a Site-2 (git-commit-phase.sh) mechanism into Site-3 (git-commit-scoped.sh) must translate warn() calls to this script's own inline-echo convention, not copy warn() verbatim.

test-git-commit-phase.sh's build_repo() fixture copies the REAL git-commit-scoped.sh (not a stub) into <repo>/.claude/scripts/git-commit-scoped.sh for every case in that suite. This means any fix landed in git-commit-scoped.sh's own source-store copy is automatically exercised end-to-end by test-git-commit-phase.sh's existing cases without needing a separate stub-update step -- a case whose own comment says it 'deliberately does not assert the end-to-end outcome because Site 3 is unpatched' can have that narrowing lifted once Site 3 is patched, no fixture change required.
